sample_description: 7,624 U.S. adults recruited on Prolific (>=95% approval, >=50 prior tasks), gender-balanced by design and deliberately skewed young (quota 40% 18-35, 40% 36-54, 20% 55-90), and SCREENED TO CLIMATE-CHANGE BELIEVERS at recruitment - so base rates are far more pro-climate and more Democratic (56% Democrat, 13% Republican) than a census-quota panel. A climate intervention tournament: 17 theory-driven interventions plus a no-intervention control (n = 850; interventions n = 370-428). Each respondent then rated 5 climate news headlines drawn from a pool of 26 New York Times articles, 3 petitions drawn from a pool of 10 adapted from Change.org, 12 everyday pro-environmental actions, 8 climate emotions, and several 1-5 attitude scales. All outcomes below are collapsed to ONE value per respondent (mean over the stimuli/items that person saw).

msg_share_broad.question: Broadcast sharing intention for climate news headlines, mean over the 5 headlines the respondent saw: 'I would share this message by posting on social media (on Facebook, Twitter/X, etc).' 0 = strongly disagree, 100 = strongly agree

msg_share_narrow.question: Narrowcast sharing intention for climate news headlines: 'I would share this message directly with someone I know (via email, direct message, etc).' 0-100

msg_rel_self.question: Perceived self-relevance of the climate news headlines: 'This message is relevant to me.' 0-100

msg_rel_social.question: Perceived social relevance of the climate news headlines: 'This message is relevant to people I know.' 0-100

petition_sign_intention.question: Petition signing intention, mean over the 3 petitions shown: 'I would sign this petition.' 0-100

petition_share_broad.question: Broadcast sharing intention for the petitions: 'I would share this petition by posting on social media.' 0-100

petition_share_narrow.question: Narrowcast sharing intention for the petitions: 'I would share this petition directly with someone I know.' 0-100

petition_sign.question: Actual petition signing: proportion of the 3 petitions the respondent chose to sign ('yes' vs no / not now / unsure). 0-1, so 1 pp = 1 percentage point of petitions signed

petition_link_clicks.question: Number of petition links (0-3) the respondent actually clicked through to

action_intention.question: Pro-environmental behaviour intentions, mean over 12 actions: 'In the future, do you intend to do this action more or less than you currently do?' 1 = a lot less, 7 = a lot more; harmful actions (driving, flying, beef/lamb) already reverse-scored

action_env_impact.question: Perceived environmental impact, mean over 12 actions: 'If many people did this action more/less often, how much would it help to reduce the negative effects of climate change?' 1 = no impact, 7 = very large impact

self_efficacy.question: Self-efficacy scale, mean of 4 items (two reverse-scored, already applied): individuals can make a difference / we cannot do anything* / there are actions I can take / it is a waste of time*. 1-5 agreement

concern_risk.question: Concern and perceived risk, mean of 4 items: concerned about climate change / important to take action / poses risks to me / poses risks to society. 1-5 agreement

emo_angry.question: 'When I think about climate change, I feel... Angry' 1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree

emo_anxious.question: 'When I think about climate change, I feel... Anxious' 1-5

emo_sad.question: 'When I think about climate change, I feel... Sad' 1-5

emo_hopeful.question: 'When I think about climate change, I feel... Hopeful' 1-5

emo_hopeless.question: 'When I think about climate change, I feel... Hopeless' 1-5

emo_determined.question: 'When I think about climate change, I feel... Determined' 1-5

emo_disengaged.question: 'When I think about climate change, I feel... Disengaged' 1-5

emo_uncertain.question: 'When I think about climate change, I feel... Uncertain' 1-5

distance_geographic.question: Geographic/self psychological distance from climate change, mean of 4 items (two reverse-scored, already applied); HIGHER = MORE DISTANT. 1-5

distance_social.question: Social psychological distance from climate change; HIGHER = MORE DISTANT. 1-5

distance_temporal.question: Temporal distance: 'When, if at all, do you think the United States will start feeling the effects of climate change?' 1 = we are already feeling the effects, 7 = never

caveats: NO INTERVENTION TEXT EXISTS ON DISK. A blind predictor sees only the 17 manuscript arm titles plus the sample and outcome descriptions. This makes bbprime2025 a task about priors over intervention FAMILIES, not about reading message copy.

Arm display names are the Rmd's own manuscript labels, taken POSITIONALLY from tournament_analysis_OSF.Rmd (factor levels c('self_relevance',...,'STPB') relabelled to c('News Comments (Self-Rel)',...,'Personal Benefits')). notes/DATA_experiments.md sec 4.2 lists that label list in the REVERSE order; the mapping used here is the Rmd's and is confirmed semantically (self_relevance->Self-Rel, STPB->Personal Benefits, CF_general->Carbon Footprint (General)).

Non-independence is structural and is NOT modelled here: 5 headlines, 3 petitions and 12 actions per person, each a separate row. The authors fit lmer/brm with random intercepts for people AND stimuli; this adapter collapses to one value per SID first, so these ATEs are person-level means, not the paper's model-based contrasts, and the SEs ignore stimulus sampling.

The sample is Prolific, screened to climate-change believers, gender-balanced by design and deliberately young-skewed (mean age 39.5), and 56% Democrat / 13% Republican. Base rates and effect sizes should NOT be ported to a census-quota panel.
Tournament-wide comparisons were not preregistered (SOP says so explicitly); only the per-intervention analyses were.

Outcome set = exactly the 24 dependent variables that tournament_analysis_OSF.Rmd runs a condition contrast on. Deliberately excluded: msg_read, msg_emo_pos, msg_emo_neg, action_ease, action_approval, action_person_impact, climate_knowledge, uncertainty, climate_change_cause, action_current* (no Rmd contrast, or no fixed scale). uncertainty is additionally truncated by design because a mean > 4 on it was an EXCLUSION criterion.

Main exclusion variant used (N = 7,624). The *_few_excl variants (N = 7,767, which re-admit climate-change deniers) were NOT used and were not needed: the party/ideology moderators ship in the MAIN other_dvs_data.csv under scale_name == 'politics' (7,620 of 7,624 have an affiliation), contradicting notes/DATA_experiments.md sec 4.4 which says they exist only in indiv_diffs_data_few_excl.csv.
petition_sign is labelled 'Post-Hoc' in the Rmd, and it is a proportion of 3 petitions (0-1), so 1 pp = 1 percentage point of petitions signed. petition_link_clicks is a 0-3 count.
distance_temporal is 1-7 while the other two distance scales are 1-5; it has 111 missing values (1.5%).
value_z was never used: it is a within-item z-score and has no percentage-point interpretation.
No survey weights exist for this study, so all ATEs are unweighted (as in the source paper).

The four 'News Comments' / relevance-targeting effects on the message-rating outcomes are large (13-16 pp) because those interventions manipulate exactly what the message items ask about; the rest of the 408-cell table is in the -4.5 to +9 pp range.

harness_note: ssb.task.true_ates does int(np.nan) when a moderator x arm x outcome cell has <=2 observations, so moderator='education' raises ValueError here. Workaround if an education-moderated carve is needed: fold 'No formal education'/'Did not complete high school' into 'High school diploma / GED' (loses the target's 'Less than high school' level).
